item.title: Senior Legal Affairs Specialist, P-5, FT, Office of Executive Director, NYHQ, PAT 113908
item.description: We seek to hire an experienced Senior Legal Affairs Specialist on a fixed-term appointment to join the Legal Team in our New York Office. item.title: Chief Supply and Logistics, (P-4), FT, #00118872, Port Au Prince, Haiti – LACR
item.description: UNICEF Haiti is seeking a results-driven Chief Supply and Logistics to lead and oversee supply chain operations in support of the Country Office’s emergency response. You will also provide strategic technical guidance and advisory support to government counterparts, national systems and partners, while driving innovation and strengthening the efficiency, effectiveness and responsiveness of supply chain operations.If you are a strategic leader with strong supply chain expertise and a passion for making a difference for children in Haiti, we would love to hear from you!

item.title: Stretch Assignment - Deputy Representative Operation, Accra Ghana
item.description:
UNICEF Ghana Country Office is seeking an experienced and dynamic UNICEF colleague for a three-month Stretch Assignment as Deputy Representative, Operations, P-4, based in Accra, Ghana.
Under the supervision of the Representative, the incumbent will provide strategic leadership and management oversight of the Operations function during a critical transition period, ensuring continuity of essential operational services and supporting the effective completion of the 2026 year-end closure and a strong start to the 2027 management cycle.
The assignment offers a unique opportunity to strength their experience in financial stewardship, enterprise risk management, audit and assurance, operational efficiency, digital transformation, business continuity, Programme-Operations collaboration, UN common services and strategic management

item.title: Programme Manager, P-4, TA (6months), #139073, Bunia, Democratic Republic of Congo-WCAR
item.description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is responding to its 17th Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) outbreak, confirmed in May 2026 and affecting Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu provinces. The situation remains complex and evolving, with transmission occurring in both community and health-care settings. Response efforts are led by national authorities in a context shaped by health system limitations, logistical constraints, insecurity, displacement, and diverse community perceptions influencing health-seeking behaviors. UNICEF supports the Government through a multi-sectoral approach, focusing on community engagement, surveillance, infection prevention, and the continuity of essential services for vulnerable populations. This context requires strong coordination, adaptability, and cultural sensitivity to support effective and equitable response efforts, particularly for children and at-risk communities.

item.title: Batch recruitment: Supply & Logistics Specialist, P-3, Temporary Position, 364 Days, Copenhagen, Denmark #00139157, #00139088
item.description: Effective operationalization of the UN80 Integrated Supply Chain Initiative will strengthen UNICEF’s contribution to a more integrated, efficient and interoperable UN supply chain. Clear operational documents and regular monitoring of key performance indicators will support consistent implementation and give senior management a reliable view of progress and results. Close alignment between the initiative and Supply Division Procurement Centers, together with improved internal procurement processes, will help UNICEF adapt as the initiative expands to more commodities and countries. Practical support to starter countries and to the scale-up of the initiative will help translate UN80 strategies into tangible results, including reduced duplication, lower costs and more reliable delivery of supplies and services to the populations the UN serves, and will position UNICEF as a trusted partner in UN supply chain reform.

item.title: Deputy Director Evaluation, D-1, Evaluation Office, Rome, Italy
item.description: UNICEF’s evaluation function is largely decentralized. The Office works closely with senior regional evaluation advisers and multi-country evaluation specialists based in each of UNICEF’s five regions, as well as dedicated country-level evaluation focal points who provide full- or part-time support to evaluation efforts. The shared goal is, to ensure together a well-coordinated, collaborative, whole-of-organization evaluation effort and to continue to build the Organization’s community of practice. The function undertakes a diverse portfolio of independent, credible, and impartial evaluations, including corporate thematic, institutional effectiveness, humanitarian, country-led, and impact evaluations. The Evaluation function aims to deliver consistent, timely, credible and useful independent analyses that harness knowledge to help UNICEF use evaluation evidence to enhance its effectiveness and overall to deliver better results for children.

item.title: Senior Expert I - Corporate Risk and Benchmarking, 9.40 months, Evaluation Office, New York, REMOTELY (Open For International Candidates), Req#596756
item.description: The UNICEF Evaluation Office (EO) is commissioning a global evaluation of UNICEF’s risk governance frameworks and practices in humanitarian action. Building on a set of case studies conducted across different emergency contexts, the evaluation will allow tracing the decision-making processes that led to either action or no action during past emergency responses and will attempt to measure their repercussion on the delivery of services and good to children, especially those in hard-to-reach areas. The evaluation aims to put forward recommendations that will equip UNICEF staff across a variety of emergency contexts to manage, prevent and share risks more responsibly and effectively in the future. The EO is seeking a Corporate Risk Benchmarking Expert for this evaluation.
